added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs: repair-base-suite.log (12b5f3d1ce) ends '6 passed' with EXIT=0 and repair-after-suite.log (5c474bd0e8) ends '7 passed' with EXIT=0, both declaring completed, so no failure appears at the head that the base did not carry.

findings.text: the `(?:` `\./` `)*` prefix is free to start one character into a `../` prefix, since re.findall resumes scanning at the second dot, so a sentence naming `../docs/x.md` derives `docs/x.md` - an in-repo path whose parent exists, which the queue-time check at :321-330 therefore accepts - where the previous pattern derived `/docs/x.md`; both are wrong, but the new value is silently accepted, which is the failure class this section guards, and no case covers the form.

`assert ABSOLUTE_RECORD.startswith("/")` compares the test's own module literal against itself and cannot fail for any behaviour of the code under test, so it adds no coverage to case one; already recorded by the prior review at head 12b5f3d1ce and unchanged by this commit.

the rewritten Measure paragraph reports that 'the head tree 20 passed' for the importer arm, but the log it names, logs/importers-after.log, declares `# revision: 12b5f3d1ce37ce5b0a5e5736a47fbefa4ad175c1` - one commit before the reviewed head - so the arm is not evidenced at 5c474bd0e8; the four other importer test files derive only plain relative paths (`src/module.py`, `one.py`, `three.py`), so the residual risk is nil, but the receipt names a revision it did not run at.
